items.quote: The River Thames, known alternatively in parts as the River Isis, is a river that flows through southern England including London.
The Great Fire of London occurred from Sunday 2 September to Wednesday 5 September 1666
Big Ben is the nickname for the Great Bell of the Great Clock of Westminster
items.note: The same sentence goes on 'and, by extension, for the clock tower', and the article says the name is now often used for the bell, clock and tower collectively. The word 'strictly' in the question is what makes 'the great bell' the one answer; keep it.

items.quote: The London Underground (also known simply as the Underground or as the Tube) is a rapid transit system serving Greater London
Nelson's Column is a monument in Trafalgar Square in the City of Westminster
The high-domed present structure, which was completed in 1710, is a Grade I listed building that was designed in the English Baroque style by Sir Christopher Wren.
The term Cockney is also used as a demonym for a person from London's East End, or, traditionally, born within earshot of Bow Bells.
popularly known as the Beefeaters, are ceremonial guardians of the Tower of London
items.note: The Yeomen of the Guard (a separate corps) share the nickname, but the question names the Tower's Yeomen Warders, so the answer is unaffected.

items.quote: 10 Downing Street in London is the official residence and office of the prime minister of the United Kingdom
items.note: Minor: Chequers is also an official (country) residence, but asking for a street address rules it out. Accept 'Number 10'.
London was also awarded 1944, cancelled for the war; 'hosted' correctly excludes it, but expect someone to raise it.
